page: Microsoft Azure E8-4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.35 GHz. The architecture is x86_64. The instance features 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It includes 131 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25%, while Geekbench single-core and image processing benchmarks score in the average range. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average for read operations at 39.48 GB/sec, but weak for write operations at 22.76 GB/sec.

The high memory density relative to the low vCPU count makes this instance qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring large memory footprints without intensive parallel processing. Tradeoffs include limited multi-threaded performance and lower throughput for database operations and static web serving, both of which benchmarked in the bottom 25%. This server is best suited for memory-bound applications with low parallel compute requirements, such as small-scale caching layers, light database tasks, or memory-intensive single-threaded processing.
